newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lower financial costs, synergy help Enso.
newsitem.headline: Lower financial costs, synergy help Enso.

text.p: Jukka Harmala, CEO of forestry group Enso, said on Tuesday lower financial costs and earlier- than-planned gains from a merger with Finnish group Veitsiluoto last year had helped its Q1 profit beat market forecasts.

"Net interest-bearing debts have fallen," Harmala told a news conference after Enso's Q1 report. He also told Reuters Financial Television that Enso's financial costs usually came down with a time-lag after interest rates fall.

When asked how Enso's Q1 earnings at 480 million could have surpassed analysts' forecasts -- the median had been around 350 million markka in a 260-470 million range -- he added that savings on its Veitsiluoto merger may have been missed.
"(Analysts) could not take into account enough the effects of the synergy benefits," he told the news conference, adding that merger benefits had come faster than Enso expected.
